## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design end-to-end tenant onboarding with real-world constraints: dynamic provisioning, GitOps integration, security gates, cost controls, drift detection, and reliable rollback. It combines AKS, Key Vault, App Configuration, and policy-driven governance in a single pipeline.

## Key Concepts
- Dynamic tenant provisioning from a registry
- Per-tenant Kubernetes namespaces and RBAC
- GitOps workflow for manifests
- Canary rollout and traffic gating
- Security gates: Kyverno policies, Trivy image scans
- Cost management gating with approvals
- Drift detection and auto-rollback
- Centralized observability with Azure Monitor Logs

## Code Example

```yaml
name: OnboardTenant
trigger: none
jobs:
- job: Onboard
  steps:
  - script: |
      echo "Register tenant from registry"
  - script: |
      echo "Create namespace and RBAC"
  - script: |
      echo "Fetch Key Vault secrets & App Configuration"
  - script: |
      echo "Apply manifests via GitOps"
  - script: |
      echo "Canary rollout and gates (Kyverno/Trivy)"
  - script: |

  - script: |

```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates real-world multi-tenant deployment patterns, including per-tenant isolation, feature flag management, and automated quality gates in enterprise environments.

## Key Concepts

- Azure DevOps YAML pipelines
- AKS with per-tenant namespaces
- App Configuration for feature flags
- k6 synthetic testing
- Azure Monitor logging
- Per-tenant promotion gates with automated rollback

## Code Example

```yaml
name: MultiTenantCanary
trigger: none
stages:
- stage: Deploy
  jobs:
  - deployment: DeployTenant
    strategy:
      matrix:
        tenantA: { tenant: 'tenant-a' }
        tenantB: { tenant: 'tenant-b' }
    environment: 'aks-${tenant}'
    pool:
      vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
    strategy:
      runOnce:
        deploy:
          steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Deploy to AKS namespace'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az aks get-credentials --resource-group $(rgName) --name $(aksCluster)
                kubectl set image deployment/api api=$(containerImage) --namespace=$(tenant)
          - task: AzureAppConfiguration@1
            displayName: 'Fetch feature flags'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
              appConfigurationResourceGroup: '$(rgName)'
              appConfigurationName: '$(appConfigName)'
              label: '$(tenant)'
          - task: Bash@3
            displayName: 'Run k6 synthetic tests'
            env:
              TENANT_URL: 'https://$(tenant).api.example.com'
            inputs:
              filePath: 'tests/k6-synthetic.sh'
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Check health and gate promotion'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                HEALTH=$(curl -s https://$(tenant).api.example.com/health)
                if [ "$HEALTH" != "healthy" ]; then
                  echo "##vso[task.logissue type=error]Health check failed for $(tenant)"
                  exit 1
                fi
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Rollback on failure'
            condition: failed()
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                kubectl rollout undo deployment/api --namespace=$(tenant)
                echo "Rolled back $(tenant) to previous revision"
          - task: AzureMonitor@1
            displayName: 'Log to Azure Monitor'
            inputs:
              azureResourceGroup: '$(rgName)'
              resourceType: 'Container Insights'
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Assesses practical skills wiring a Terraform workflow into Azure DevOps: secret retrieval, per-PR state isolation, plan-only validation, and drift checks without risking production.

## Key Concepts

- Azure DevOps YAML pipelines and PR triggers
- Terraform init with Azure backend and per-PR state files
- Azure Key Vault for deployment secrets
- Plan-only validation in PR context; artifact/PR comment delivery
- Drift/diff check in a separate job

## Code Example

```javascript
trigger: none
pr:
  branches:
    include:
      - main
variables:
  tfstate_key: 'tfstate-PR-${{ System.PullRequest.PullRequestId }}'
jobs:
  - job: Plan
    pool:
      vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
    steps:
      - task: AzureKeyVault@2
        inputs:
          connectedServiceName: 'AzureSPN'
          keyVaultName: 'infrakv'
          secretsFilter: 'DEPLOYMENT_KEY'
      - script: |
          terraform init \
            -backend-config="resource_group_name=tfstate" \
            -backend-config="storage_account_name=mytfstate" \
            -backend-config="container_name=tfstate" \
            -backend-config="key=${tfstate_key}"
          terraform fmt
          terraform validate
          terraform plan -out=tfplan
        displayName: 'Plan'
      - task: PublishBuildArtifacts@1
        inputs:
          pathToPublish: 'tfplan'
          artifactName: 'terraform-plan'
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you extend this to support multiple environments (dev/stage/prod)?
- How would you automatically comment the plan back to the PR and fail if there are changes?

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates a candidate's ability to design a CI/CD pipeline that enforces governance gates before deployment while enabling rapid feedback through ephemeral environments.

## Key Concepts
- Azure Policy integration as a CI/CD gate
- AKS ephemeral namespace deployment
- Helm-based deployments with per-environment configuration
- Azure Key Vault and Azure App Configuration integration
- Health checks and automatic rollback mechanisms
- Azure Monitor logging for traceability

## Code Example
```yaml
trigger:
  branches:
    include:
      - main
pr: none

stages:
  - stage: Build
    jobs:
      - job: BuildAndTest
        pool:
          vmImage: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - task: NodeTool@0
            inputs:
              versionSpec: '20.x'
          - script: npm install && npm test
  
  - stage: PolicyCheck
    jobs:
      - job: AKSComplianceCheck
        steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION)
              script: |
                az policy state list \
                  --resource-group $(AKS_RESOURCE_GROUP) \
                  --filter "complianceState eq 'NonCompliant'"
  
  - stage: Deploy
    dependsOn: PolicyCheck
    jobs:
      - job: DeployToEphemeralNS
        steps:
          - task: HelmInstaller@1
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            script: |
              NAMESPACE="pr-$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestId)"
              helm upgrade --install $NAMESPACE ./chart \
                --namespace $NAMESPACE --create-namespace \
                --set env=$(DEPLOYMENT_ENV)
  
  - stage: Validate
    jobs:
      - job: HealthCheck
        steps:
          - script: |
              curl -f http://$NAMESPACE.health || exit 1
      - job: RollbackOnFailure
        condition: failed()
        steps:
          - script: helm uninstall $NAMESPACE
```

## Why This Is Asked
Assesses end-to-end CI/CD workflows in a PR-driven environment with containerization, basic Kubernetes operations, and observability. Key emphases include reproducible builds, environment isolation, simple health checks, and resource cleanup to prevent leakage.

## Key Concepts

- npm tasks (install, test, lint)
- Docker image building and pushing
- Azure Container Registry (ACR)
- Azure CLI for AKS cluster management
- kubectl for Kubernetes deployments and services
- Manual and automatic resource cleanup
- Azure Monitor logging integration

## Code Example
```yaml
trigger: none
pr:
  - main
pool:
  vmImage: ubuntu-latest

stages:
  - stage: Build
    jobs:
      - job: BuildAndTest
        steps:
          - task: NodeTool@0
            inputs:
              versionSpec: '18.x'
          - script: npm ci
            displayName: 'Install dependencies'
          - script: npm test
            displayName: 'Run unit tests'
          - script: npm run lint
            displayName: 'Run ESLint'
          - task: Docker@2
            inputs:
              command: buildAndPush
              repository: '$(ACR_LOGIN_SERVER)/app:$(Build.BuildId)'
              dockerfile: '$(Build.SourcesDirectory)/Dockerfile'
              containerRegistry: '$(ACR_SERVICE_CONNECTION)'

  - stage: Deploy
    dependsOn: Build
    condition: and(succeeded(), eq(variables['Build.Reason'], 'PullRequest'))
    jobs:
      - deployment: DeployToAKS
        environment: 'aks-pr-$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestNumber)'
        strategy:
          runOnce:
            deploy:
              steps:
                - task: AzureCLI@2
                  inputs:
                    azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION)'
                    scriptType: 'bash'
                    scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
                    inlineScript: |
                      PR_ID=$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestNumber)
                      NAMESPACE="pr-$PR_ID"
                      kubectl create namespace $NAMESPACE --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
                      kubectl set image deployment/app app=$(ACR_LOGIN_SERVER)/app:$(Build.BuildId) -n $NAMESPACE
                      kubectl expose deployment/app --type=LoadBalancer --port=80 --target-port=3000 -n $NAMESPACE
                      sleep 30
                      SERVICE_IP=$(kubectl get svc app -n $NAMESPACE -o jsonpath='{.status.loadBalancer.ingress[0].ip}')
                      curl -f http://$SERVICE_IP/health || exit 1
                - task: AzureMonitor@1
                  inputs:
                    alertResourceGroup: '$(RESOURCE_GROUP)'
                    metricsResourceID: '$(AZURE_MONITOR_RESOURCE_ID)'
```
